verses.author: model_A
verses.text: An orchard planted by a man who never tasted its fruit.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text: Grandchildren spit the seeds where his shadow used to fall.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Small trees rising where the seeds took root,
patient the way he was, without complaint.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The rain doesn't ask whose hands did the planting,
falls the same on all the rows.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Someone still walks the rows counting blossoms,
naming each one for a hand that isn't there.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The names don't stick to the branches long—
wind takes them before the frost can.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Even so she whispers them each morning,
small offerings the wind can have, if it must.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
What the wind takes, it doesn't waste—
listen close, that's her voice still moving through the leaves.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
A single leaf breaks loose and spirals down—
someone below reaches up, calling it by name.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The name lands wrong, palm-up, empty—
still, he folds his hand around the air it left.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
He carries that fist all the way home,
opens it at the door like a small gift for no one.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
No one is home, but the room hears it anyway—
a cup already set on the table, waiting.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Steam rises from a kettle no one boiled—
the window fogs with someone else's breath.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone else's breath clears from the glass slow,
leaving the street exactly as it was, minus one shape.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Minus one shape, the porch light still keeps watch—
moths circling a welcome nobody remembers giving.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Nobody remembers giving, yet the door stays unlocked—
a key still warm in the pocket of a coat on the hook.
